answer.text: The total risk of the stock
The systematic or market risk of the stock relative to the overall market
The dividend yield of the stock
The PE ratio relative to the market PE

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the NISM Series XV Research Analyst workbook (pages 238-239), beta measures the sensitivity of a stock's returns to index/market returns and is used to assess systematic (market) risk. A beta of 1 means the stock moves in line with the market; a beta less than 1 means it is less volatile than the market; a beta greater than 1 means it is more volatile than the market. The Trap: Option A confuses beta with total risk, but beta captures only the systematic, market-driven component, not unsystematic risk. Options C and D describe income yield and relative valuation, which are unrelated to beta. Note: When reading a beta value, compare it to 1 and interpret direction and magnitude of co-movement with the market index rather than treating it as an overall risk or valuation indicator.
